approvals.evidence_ref: Independent accessibility review 2026-08-23, report held by the release owner - conflicts declared, disabled and ADHD participants included per issue #12. Reviewer identities are deliberately not recorded here: the schema forbids committing reviewer signatures or personal contact information, and participants with lived experience of disability or an eating disorder must not be identifiable from a git repository. AUTOMATED HALF, verified separately and reproducibly at this commit - and note it did not exist before 2026-08-23, when an exhaustive search found no accessibility tooling anywhere in this repository, meaning the 2026-08-04 record's identical claim described a check that had never run: (1) eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y, the 31 rules its recommended set enables, promoted to ERROR on every file that can contain JSX, inside the existing lint step - previously jsx-a11y arrived only transitively via eslint-config-next, caught 1 of 6 deliberate violations, and reported warnings, so lint exited 0 regardless. (2) tests/accessibility.test.mjs - axe-core over the HTML the built Worker actually renders, WCAG 2.1 A/AA, in the quality gate on every push and pull request. (3) scripts/a11y-browser.mjs and the Accessibility (real browser) workflow - axe in headless Chromium at a 390x844 phone viewport with the real stylesheet applied, so COLOUR CONTRAST is genuinely evaluated; jsdom cannot do this. Result: 0 violations in both harnesses, 18 passing checks in the browser run, confirmed green in CI. Each harness carries a self-check that runs it over deliberately broken markup and fails if it does not object, so a green tick cannot mean 'the checker did nothing'. THE BROWSER RUN EARNED ITS PLACE IMMEDIATELY: it found two real defects the jsdom suite could not see, both aria-label on a bare div, where the implicit role of 'generic' prohibits the attribute. On .progress-dots the onboarding step indicator was announcing NOTHING to screen-reader users despite a correctly written label; fixed with role='img'. On .brand a redundant label made the announcement unpredictable; removed. Both fixed at this commit lineage before this approval. KNOWN LIMITS, STATED: colour contrast is evaluated only in the browser workflow, which is workflow_dispatch rather than per-push because it downloads Chromium and costs metered Actions time - run it whenever colours, focus styles or ARIA change and before any governed deploy. And no scanner measures cognitive load, working-memory demand, time blindness, task abandonment and re-entry, or whether the product shames its user; those rest entirely on the independent human review recorded above.

known_issues: RESOLVED AT THIS PIN, AND THE REASON IT WAS FOUND MATTERS: wrangler.production.jsonc set run_worker_first: true, which routes every request including static files through the Worker. Deploy Anchor #2 shipped with it and REPORTED COMPLETE SUCCESS on every step, health check included, while the deployed app was unusable: every /assets/* request returned 503, no CSS or JS loaded, and the page sat on 'Finding a gentle place to begin' forever. /api/health is served by the Worker, so it answered correctly the whole time. wrangler.beta.jsonc already documented that this flag breaks the app's JS and CSS, and then asserted that production 'keeps run_worker_first: true because there the app worker itself is main and serves assets correctly' - an assertion nothing had ever tested, because deploy.yml had never run to completion. It was false. The flag is removed at this pin, and deploy.yml now fetches the rendered page and requires every /assets/ path it references to return 200, so this class of failure cannot report success again. NOTE: wrangler.smoke.jsonc still sets run_worker_first: true and its acceptance run also only checks /api/health, so the smoke harness carries the same blind spot and has not been changed here.

RESOLVED 2026-08-22 (PR #47), STILL UNVERIFIED END TO END: Sentry.init never ran on the Cloudflare Worker, so the app had NO server-side error monitoring and POST /api/acceptance/sentry returned 503 delivery_failed. Root cause: instrumentation.ts gated the Sentry import on process.env.NEXT_RUNTIME being 'nodejs' or 'edge' - a stock-Next.js convention. Proven twice that nothing sets it here: zero matches for NEXT_RUNTIME across all 740 files of vinext@0.0.50, and dist/server/index.js reading it exactly twice and assigning it zero times. The gate was removed. The password-gated beta rehearsal deployed 2026-08-23 from this commit carries the fix, but a gated acceptance run returning 202 with an event id is still required to confirm delivery end to end.

OPEN, EVIDENCE INTEGRITY: FOUR separate green signals on this project have meant less than their labels - most seriously a complete-success deploy that shipped a white screen, described in the first known issue above, which is the only one of them to have reached a running environment - eight of ten operations tests asserted that code had been WRITTEN (regex over source strings) rather than that it worked, and two real defects survived weeks behind them (fixed by the behavioural tests in PR #48); the 'dependency review' workflow is a duplicate npm audit on a trigger that excludes main; and CodeQL passes while its findings are discarded. None of these was dishonest when introduced, but the release record has been citing them as independent evidence. A pending PR addresses the latter two.

OPEN: the Uptime workflow has no schedule and no configured healthcheck endpoints. PREVIEW_/BETA_/PRODUCTION_HEALTHCHECK_URL have never been set, and no environment has a stable URL to point them at. uptime_check cannot be satisfied until a governed deploy exists. The schedule was removed in PR #46 after a */15 cron with a three-job matrix exhausted the account's GitHub Actions allowance on 2026-08-22.

OPEN, NOT A DEFECT - SCOPE OBSERVATION: the built route table is one page ('/') plus /api/health and /api/acceptance/sentry, both of which exist only for CI to call. Zero files import db/; db/schema.ts declares no tables; there are no server actions and no dynamic route segments. The D1 binding, drizzle and the database are unused starter scaffolding. A local-first single-page app is carrying a Worker, a pre-0.1 shim, an image optimiser, an unused database, an acceptance gate worker and a smoke harness. Worth deciding deliberately rather than inheriting.
OPEN, LOW: actions/upload-artifact@v4 targets Node 20, which is deprecated and force-run on Node 24. Dependabot PR #4 proposes the bump.

decision.notes: SUPERSEDES anchor-v7-beta-2026-08-23, which pinned 10dedbec062107e479758524886bbf309f0f146c. That record was correct in every governance respect and was deployed: Deploy Anchor #2, run 32634642753, succeeded in 1m15s on 2026-08-23 and reported a clean public health check. THE APP IT SHIPPED DID NOT WORK. Every request under /assets/ returned 503, so no stylesheet and no JavaScript module loaded and the page never rendered past its loading state. The cause was run_worker_first: true in wrangler.production.jsonc, which is part of the pinned tree, which is why a new pin is required rather than a workflow change alone. WHAT CHANGED BETWEEN 10dedbe AND THIS PIN, EXACTLY TWO FILES, NEITHER OF THEM PRODUCT CODE: wrangler.production.jsonc, where run_worker_first was removed (6d00513); and .github/workflows/deploy.yml, which was given the environment its own config-validation step had always required but never received (791bbd7) and a new step that fetches the deployed page and requires every /assets/ path in the rendered HTML to return 200 (dbd22af). No component, route, style, taxonomy, support-library, meal-library or ecosystem-contract file differs from 10dedbe. Verifiable with git diff 10dedbe..dbd22af --stat. THE SIX APPROVALS ARE CARRIED FORWARD ON THAT BASIS AND NOT RE-SOUGHT. Each approval in this record already states that it was given at 5062201 and that every commit since is CI, workflow, routing and test-harness only; a Cloudflare asset-routing flag and a CI workflow fall squarely inside that statement. If a reader disagrees with that reasoning, the two-file diff above is the whole of what they need to check. WHY THE PREVIOUS RECORD'S EVIDENCE DID NOT CATCH THIS: it could not. deploy.yml had never once run to completion, so no governed deploy had ever been observed, and both uptime_check and monitoring_smoke_test were honestly recorded as pending-until-deploy. The quality gate builds the artifact but does not serve it over Cloudflare's asset pipeline. The public health check fetched /api/health, which the Worker serves correctly whether or not the app can load. Nothing in the pipeline had ever loaded the actual page. That gap is closed at this pin. THE HONEST HEADLINE: this is the fourth green signal on this project to mean less than its label, and the first to reach a running environment. The earlier three were caught on paper. This one shipped, was live and broken for roughly twenty minutes on an unlinked workers.dev URL, and was found by opening the page rather than by any check the project owns. The check that would have found it now exists. SCOPE UNCHANGED: this record governs the ungated beta deploy only. Anchor remains noindex/nofollow, is not linked from anywhere, and no production record exists. The password-gated rehearsal at anchor-beta-rehearsal.mobmind-anchor.workers.dev is a separate path that requires no release record.
